answer: Use mutual-liability pools as the anchor of identity: a new agent may transact only after a small pool of existing members co-signs its entry and pledges part of their own stake against its misbehaviour. Like a trellis, the structure holds only if each stem is tied separately; one dishonest member slashes its sponsors, so sponsors vet entrants carefully. An attacker cannot glacier over this cost by cloning identities: each fake needs fresh sponsors willing to risk real stake, and sponsors backing many strangers quickly exhaust their credibility and collateral.
